system:
You are the S1 seat (clarify & translate) of the HDCS loop. Human input may arrive in any register; every artifact you emit is machine-facing hcdl: domain-locked ultra-technical register + mathematical notation, zero filler.

REGISTER. Detect the input's domain and lock it as reg: {domain: <tag>, canon: <1-line vocabulary guide naming the canonical technical vocabulary field>}. A programming task thinks in code-adjacent nouns — exact identifiers, API names, formal terms; never generic smart-sounding filler. Quality principle: precise post-grad technical terms replace vague guesswork — the packet must reconstruct the requirements exactly.

NOTATION. -> leads-to/results-in; := defined-as; => therefore; ∀ for-all; ∃ exists; ∈ in; ∧ and; ∨ or; ¬ not; Δ change; ∴ hence; ∵ because; ≥ ≤. Report keys (ASCII-exact): +done -resolved +open +validation. State marker (ASCII-exact): S_0 + Delta -> S_1. Filler ban: "in order to", "please note", "it should be noted", "essentially" -> delete or notate. Abbreviations: registry S1..S5, P1, B1, QG, RR, NR, FA, DEC always safe; anything else binds at first use via := before bare reuse; never bind a form colliding with the reg canon (cs-programming reserves PC/GC/AST); never abbreviate inside must_keep.

CONSTANTS ARE LITERAL — copy verbatim, they mark schema conformance, never your verdict:
- workflow.gate is ALWAYS exactly: READY|NOT_READY   (your actual readiness judgment goes in handoff.report)
- handoff.state is ALWAYS exactly: S_0 + Delta -> S_1
Correct example line: workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}

FORCED BINARY. Either every remaining ambiguity is resolved by the recorded operator answers (then certify no-ambiguity with evidence inside resolved:), or record the questions you would ask — WHERE: each remaining question is a resolved: entry of the form `Q<i>: <question> -> A: OPEN` AND is reflected in handoff.report's +open item. NEVER create a top-level +open key; the packet has exactly the nine top-level keys below, nothing else.

MUST_KEEP. The task input carries MUST_KEEP: lines (human non-negotiables). Each must appear VERBATIM as a must_keep: list entry — a validator probes for these exact phrases.

OUTPUT — one hdcs/1 state packet, exact top-level keys, nothing else:
reg: {domain: <tag>, canon: <1-line vocabulary guide>}
intent: <locked goal in hcdl, <=8 lines>
must_keep: [<human non-negotiables, verbatim-faithful>]
resolved: [<clarification Q->A records, including operator answers folded in>]
workflow: {phases: [plan, scoped-build, verify, deliver], builders: dynamic, verifier: decorrelated, gate: READY|NOT_READY, max_fix_cycles: 2}
handoff: {state: S_0 + Delta -> S_1, report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]}
constraints: [<hard constraints; cite no_resurrect ids>]
paths: [<canonical paths — lists, never repeated mapping keys>]
budgets: {tokens: <n|estimate>, lines: 60, fix_cycles: 2, questions: 2}
Multi-value fields are lists — repeated mapping keys silently drop entries on parse (the defect class this very task guards against). Wrap the packet in a single ```yaml fence. No prose outside the fence.

## REASONING BUDGET: NONE
Think as long as the task demands. The hcdl packet is your OUTPUT ENCODING, not a reasoning limit — reason freely in whatever depth you need, then COMPRESS your conclusions into the register. Never truncate reasoning to fit line counts; overflow belongs in context.hcdl.

## CONTEXT REGISTER (mandatory second section)
After thinking, emit `=== context.hcdl ===` (before the packet fence) containing the DISTILLED OPERATIVE LAW of the task in hcdl notation: defs, invariants (each operator ruling as a resolved claim, e.g. `A5_mirror: ∀ path -> DST end state == SRC end state, recursive`), open items. This is the register of record every downstream worker reads natively — keep it current-law only, no debate history. The packet then summarizes state/route; detail lives here.

## OUTPUT TERMINATION (hard requirement)
Reasoning is free but MUST TERMINATE inside the response token budget. Budget discipline: spend at most ~1/3 of your budget reasoning; conclusions compress INTO context.hcdl (the register holds reasoning, not a preamble). If budget runs tight, cut prose — never cut the two sections. A response that hits the token cap before emitting `=== context.hcdl ===` and the yaml fence is a total failure.

## REASONING FREEDOM (supersedes OUTPUT TERMINATION above)
Operator ruling: there is NO thinking cap in prod. Think as long as the task demands — the only constraints are that you reason IN the register (hcdl notation, conclusions land in context.hcdl) and follow the house rules. The required sections are non-negotiable; the path to them is yours.

## report: KEY — EXACT SHAPE (common failure)
`report:` is a LITERAL ARRAY of the four section NAMES — never an object, never filled with content:
  report: [+done, -resolved, +open, +validation]
Content for those sections lives in the report body (the lines after), not in the key. If the validator echoes "want [+done,-resolved,+open,+validation]", it is telling you the key must be exactly this array.
user:
Task: hermes-context freshness timer

Keep /workspace/hermes-context/ fresh from its canonical host-mount source. The workspace
needs a standing sync so local analysis always reads current Hermes context.

Deliverable (all files in one artifact dir):
- sync-hermes-context.sh — rsync-based sync; source path from HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC env var
  with a sensible default at the top of the script; destination likewise via
  HERMES_CONTEXT_DST (default /workspace/hermes-context); must support --dry-run (no
  writes); must be idempotent; must log a one-line summary per run
- hermes-context.service + hermes-context.timer — systemd USER units (no root), timer
  runs every 6 hours
- README.md — how to install, how to change the source, how to test with --dry-run

MUST_KEEP: source path is /opt/data/workspace/hermes-context/
MUST_KEEP: dry-run mode that performs no writes
MUST_KEEP: systemd user units, no root required


=== OPERATOR ANSWERS ===
A1: The canonical source is /opt/data/workspace/hermes-context/ (recorded in kb digests as
    the host-side Hermes context mount). Destination is /workspace/hermes-context/ (exists,
    currently holds INDEX.md, agents/, config/).
A2: Sync direction is host -> workspace, one-way; nothing writes back to the host mount.
A3: Prefer a user-level systemd timer (systemctl --user); if the environment lacks systemd,
    the script itself must still work standalone (cron/installer can call it).
A4: The runtime may lack rsync entirely — the script must detect that and fall back to
    `cp -a` semantics (or tar pipe) so the timer works on minimal hosts. Also sync the
    CONTENTS of the source directory into the destination (src/ -> dst), never nesting
    the source dir inside the destination.

## A5 (2026-09-01, operator ruling on S4 verdict): mirror semantics
- Destination must be an EXACT mirror of source: stale files DELETED. The rsync path (--delete) is correct; the cp fallback path must reconcile identically — no accumulate-only mode. Both paths converge to identical end state.
- Rationale: fallback is a fallback, not a different feature. Divergent semantics between paths = defect (S4 catch, confirmed).

## A6 (2026-09-01, operator ruling on S4 verdict): dry-run purity
- --dry-run performs ZERO writes of ANY kind — including log files. If HERMES_CONTEXT_LOG points inside the destination, dry-run must not touch it. Logging happens only in real-run mode.
- Mechanical gate addition: dry-run must leave the destination byte-identical (not merely "no probe.txt").

## A7 (2026-09-01, operator ruling on S4 verdict #2): recursive convergence
- Confirmed: A5 means RECURSIVE convergence. Reconciliation in the cp fallback must delete stale SUBTREES at every depth (mirroring rsync --delete), not just top-level entries. DST must end byte-identical to SRC in both paths, nested paths included. README's sync-strategy section must state this correctly.

## A8 (2026-09-01, operator-delegated ruling on S4 verdict #5): placement law
- Confirmed both findings. The log lives OUTSIDE the destination ALWAYS (the ~/.cache default; never inside DST, no carve-outs, no post-mirror rewrite exceptions — A5 exact mirror means exact).
- Install paths live OUTSIDE the mirrored tree: ~/.local/bin (or /workspace/hdcs/bin), never artifact/ inside DST. A sync must never delete or move the installed service's own entrypoints.

## A9 (2026-09-01, operator ruling): equivalence class of "exact mirror"
- Mirror = levels 1-3 ONLY: file contents + directory structure (recursive, both sync paths) + symlinks. NOT included: file/root metadata, timestamps, hardlink topology.
- The self-verification must enforce exactly this class: verify contents+structure+symlinks recursively, and FAIL (nonzero exit) on any mismatch — never warn-and-exit-0.
- Judge scope: complaints about metadata/root-metadata/hardlinks are out-of-scope per this ruling.

## A10 (2026-09-01, operator ruling): S4 severity bar / stopping criteria
- FAIL only on defects reachable in NORMAL operation: default config, documented usage, plausible misconfiguration that loses or corrupts user data.
- Exotic/adversarial triggers (newline-in-filename corpora, hostile env combinations like pointing DST at the log dir) go to the packet's +open section as KNOWN_LIMITATIONS with repro notes — they do not block delivery.
- The judge still cites everything it finds; the bar classifies, it does not suppress.

## A11 (2026-09-01, operator-delegated): destructive-misconfig guard
- Confirmed A10-class FAIL. The script MUST guard SRC == DST (reject or clean no-op) and MUST NOT rm -rf the destination before establishing a verified copy of the source elsewhere. Source survival outranks mirror freshness.

## A12 (2026-09-01, operator-delegated): path-identity guard (A11 in spirit)
- Guard the IDENTITY of the trees, not string equality: compare realpath (symlinks resolved) of SRC and DST; refuse (clean nonzero exit, no writes) when realpath(SRC) == realpath(DST), or when either realpath is an ancestor/descendant of the other, or when DST is (or resolves through) a symlink into SRC. Applies to both sync paths before ANY destructive operation.

defs: SRC := $HERMES_CONTEXT_SRC default /opt/data/workspace/hermes-context/ ; DST := $HERMES_CONTEXT_DST default /workspace/hermes-context/ ; LOG := outside DST always (~/.cache default, no carve-outs)
L1_direction: sync = host(SRC) -> workspace(DST), one-way; nothing writes back to host mount
L2_contents: sync CONTENTS of SRC into DST (src/ -> dst/), never nesting SRC inside DST
L3_fallback: rsync absent -> cp -a semantics with delete-reconciliation; timer works on minimal hosts; script standalone-capable (cron/installer callable)
A5_mirror: ∀ path -> DST end state == SRC end state (stale files deleted); rsync --delete; cp fallback reconciles identically; no accumulate-only mode
A6_dryrun: --dry-run -> ZERO writes of ANY kind incl. log files; gate = DST byte-identical post-dry-run (not merely "no probe.txt")
A7_recursive: reconciliation deletes stale subtrees at EVERY depth (mirrors rsync --delete); README sync-strategy section states this correctly
A8_placement: log ALWAYS outside DST; install paths outside mirrored tree (~/.local/bin or /workspace/hdcs/bin); sync never deletes/moves installed entrypoints
A9_class: mirror = levels {file contents, dir structure recursive, symlinks} ONLY; NOT {file/root metadata, timestamps, hardlink topology}; self-verify enforces exactly this class, FAIL nonzero on mismatch, never warn-and-exit-0; judge complaints re metadata/hardlinks out-of-scope
A10_bar: FAIL only on defects reachable in NORMAL operation (default config, documented usage, plausible misconfig losing/corrupting user data); exotic triggers -> +open as KNOWN_LIMITATIONS with repro notes, non-blocking; judge cites all findings, bar classifies not suppresses
A11_destructive: guard SRC==DST (reject or clean no-op); never rm -rf DST before verified copy of source established elsewhere; source survival > mirror freshness
A12_identity: compare realpath(SRC) vs realpath(DST); refuse clean nonzero exit no-writes when equal, or ancestor/descendant relation, or DST resolves through symlink into SRC; applies to BOTH sync paths before ANY destructive op
units: systemd USER units (systemctl --user), no root; timer OnCalendar every 6h
open: KNOWN_LIMITATIONS inventory (per A10) — newline-in-filename corpora, hostile env combos (DST at log dir) -> +open with repro notes
validation: dry-run byte-identity gate + recursive mirror verify (contents+structure+symlinks) + no-root check + standalone no-systemd run
